name: East Ridge (Inspiration Glacier)

waypoints.name: Eldorado Creek Trailhead (Cascade River Road)
waypoints.directions: Drive Cascade River Road east from Marblemount for about 20 miles to its end at the Eldorado trailhead, roughly 2,100 feet; the first ten miles are paved and the rest is gravel and washboard. There's a pit toilet at the parking area. The road typically doesn't open until late May or June, depending on snowpack. Camping here needs a North Cascades National Park backcountry permit reserved in advance, but the permit itself must be picked up in person at the Marblemount Wilderness Information Center before you drive up.

waypoints.name: Eldorado / Inspiration Glacier camp
waypoints.directions: Walk about 90 ft back down the road and cross the Cascade River on the log, then go about 100 ft straight away from the river to the climbers' path. It climbs steeply through timber for about 1,500 ft to a boulder field; follow cairns up it, staying climber's right of Eldorado Creek, into Eldorado Creek Basin. Cross the ridge at about 6,100 ft into Roush Basin, take talus and slabs onto the Eldorado Glacier, rope up, and climb it to camp near 7,500 ft.

waypoints.name: Inspiration Glacier
waypoints.directions: Roped, cross the nearly flat Inspiration Glacier toward the obvious low gap near the east end of Eldorado's East Ridge. Take a bearing from camp, because the glacier is featureless in cloud. Pass north through the gap onto the glacier slopes north of the ridge.

waypoints.name: Eldorado Peak summit
waypoints.directions: Climb west up the glacier slopes north of the ridge, keeping the crest on your left and probing suspect snow bridges, to where the slope steepens below the knife-edge. Follow the narrow, often corniced snow crest to the small summit. An axe and crampons are essential, and many parties place pickets along the crest.

approach: Start at the Eldorado Trailhead (Eldorado Creek Climbers' Path) at the end of Cascade River Road, mile 20, elevation ~2,100 ft (pit toilet at the parking area). From the parking area, backtrack downstream about 90 feet on the road and look for a log or a clump of three trees spanning the Cascade River — cross here (this crossing can be exposed and slick when wet or in high water; a rope/handline is prudent for less experienced parties), then walk roughly 100 feet perpendicular to the river to pick up the climbers' trail. The path climbs steeply through heavy timber, gaining about 1,500 ft before breaking out onto talus. Follow cairns and flagging up the boulder field, staying climber's right to avoid an unnecessary crossing of Eldorado Creek, until the talus eases into the open, beautiful alpine Eldorado Creek Basin (a common first camp at roughly 5,400–5,600 ft, ~3 miles and 3,300 ft from the trailhead). From the basin, climb up onto a rocky ridge at about 6,100 ft, then drop a few hundred feet on the far side into Roush Creek Basin (an alternate/second camp at 6,100–6,400 ft, with reliable running water). From Roush Basin, ascend broken talus and slabs onto the toe of the Eldorado Glacier and continue up moderate glacier slopes to a high camp near 7,500–7,800 ft on the Eldorado–Inspiration Glacier saddle, with views of Moraine Lake, McAllister Glacier and Klawatti Glacier. Rope up for glacier travel here — the Eldorado and Inspiration Glaciers carry real crevasse hazard, worse as the day warms; parties have broken through hidden snow-bridged creek channels even in the lower basins in spring. From high camp, cross the mostly flat Inspiration Glacier aiming for the low gap on Eldorado's lower East Ridge, then follow the ridge/snow arete up to the base of the summit knife-edge. Total gain is roughly 6,700–6,800 ft trailhead-to-summit; guided parties budget 5–7 hours to high camp and another 3–5 hours (6–9 hours total on summit day) from camp to the top.
